description: Create the greenfield ASP.NET Core solution under app/todoapp-webapi, pin the supported .NET LTS SDK and dependency versions, run one Compose-managed Postgres with a retained volume and healthcheck, configure TODO_DB_CONNECTION with a documented local-only default, and bootstrap the tasks schema before database routes are served.

acceptance: A fresh Postgres instance creates the tasks table automatically and the API can list an empty database with HTTP 200 without manual schema setup.
The SDK, Postgres image, ASP.NET Core, Npgsql, xUnit, test SDK, and ASP.NET test-host versions are pinned and documented; no external credential is hardcoded.
Setting TODO_DB_CONNECTION changes the database target, while the absent-variable default is limited to local Compose use.
constraints: Target is app/todoapp-webapi; Compose contains only Postgres, its persistent volume, and its healthcheck.
Use one singleton NpgsqlDataSource or equivalent shared connection factory; do not add EF Core, Dapper, a generic repository, or a generic service layer.
The initial schema may use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS; schema evolution after this baseline requires a new explicit migration decision.
decisions: ADR-002: Use ASP.NET Core on a supported pinned .NET LTS version.
ADR-003: Use direct Npgsql with parameterized commands and a Postgres-generated positive bigint id.
ADR-004: Use one local Postgres service with a retained volume and healthcheck.
ADR-005: Apply the initial schema idempotently at API startup before serving database-dependent routes.
ADR-009: Read TODO_DB_CONNECTION and provide only a documented local default.
requirements: RF-007: Automatically create the required table before first use.
RF-008: Read TODO_DB_CONNECTION and use a local default only when absent.
RNF-005: Start verification only after a positive Postgres healthcheck.
RNF-011: Document supported versions and a reproducible local environment.
SEC-002: Externalize the connection and never hardcode external credentials.

title: Foundation: pinned ASP.NET Core, Postgres, configuration, and schema bootstrap

description: Implement the minimal shared kernel and HTTP error boundary: task/status representation, shared data-source registration, canonical JSON serialization, Problem Details, sanitized database-failure mapping, and local-only boundary documentation. Keep all endpoint-specific validation, SQL, and mapping in feature folders.

acceptance: Client errors use application/problem+json with type, title, status, detail, and instance; dependency failures use status 503.
A database failure exposes none of the connection string, credentials, internal host, stack trace, or driver details in the response or headers.
The public task representation exposes only id, titulo, and status, and status values are exactly pendente or concluida.
constraints: Program.cs is composition only; feature rules and SQL remain in their owning slices.
Never copy raw exceptions, SQL, connection strings, or driver messages into HTTP responses or logs.
Do not introduce identity, authentication, authorization, frontend, external exposure, or regulated-data claims.
decisions: ADR-001: Organize behavior by vertical slice and keep shared code genuinely common.
ADR-006: Restrict the shared kernel to task/status, data-source setup, and common errors.
ADR-010: Use canonical JSON fields and states, Problem Details, and 503 for database unavailability.
requirements: RNF-009: Shared code contains only the entity/status, connection/data source, and common errors.
SEC-001: Sanitize dependency failures and omit internal details.
SEC-004: Document the unauthenticated, local-only, non-production boundary.
SEC-005: Do not log titles or request payloads by default.

title: Shared kernel and sanitized HTTP error boundary

description: Implement the AddTask vertical slice for POST /tasks. Parse titulo, trim and validate it before mutation, insert a pending task with parameterized Npgsql SQL, map the persisted row, return 201 with Location, and cover pure rules plus real HTTP/Postgres behavior.

acceptance: POST /tasks with a valid title returns 201, a Location header, id, normalized titulo, and status pendente, and creates exactly one row.
Missing, empty, or whitespace-only titulo returns 400 Problem Details and creates no row.
Postgres generates a distinct positive id and leading/trailing whitespace is never persisted.
constraints: The slice owns its request/response types, validation, INSERT command, parameters, and row mapping.
Validation and normalization finish before a mutable database command is opened; use long for public id and cancellation-aware async calls.
Expose only id, titulo, and status; no uniqueness, maximum-length, authentication, or frontend behavior is added.
decisions: ADR-001: Keep HTTP, rules, SQL, and mapping co-located in the AddTask slice.
ADR-003: Use direct parameterized Npgsql rather than an ORM or repository.
ADR-010: Return the canonical task JSON and Problem Details contract.
requirements: RF-001: Create and persist a task through POST /tasks with 201 and Location.
RN-001: Require a non-empty trimmed title.
RN-002: New tasks start as pendente.
RN-003: Use a distinct increasing positive Postgres-generated id.
RN-009: Reject invalid titles atomically before mutation.
SEC-003: Validate before mutation and parameterize every database input.

title: AddTask: create normalized pending tasks

description: Implement the ListTasks vertical slice for GET /tasks and its optional status filter. Validate the filter before querying, select explicit public fields with parameterized SQL, order by ascending id, return [] for an empty database, and test both pure filtering and real HTTP/Postgres queries.

acceptance: GET /tasks returns 200 with an array containing only id, titulo, and status, ordered by ascending id; an empty database returns [].
status=pendente and status=concluida each return only the requested state, while omitting status returns all tasks.
Any status outside the two-value domain returns 400 Problem Details with no data array and causes no mutation.
constraints: The slice owns filter parsing, SELECT SQL, status parameterization, ordering, and row mapping.
Use shared status values but keep filter-specific rules in ListTasks; use cancellation-aware async database calls.
No pagination, performance, or extra query abstraction is introduced.
decisions: ADR-001: Keep listing and filtering in one cohesive vertical slice.
ADR-003: Use direct parameterized Npgsql SQL and explicit mapping.
ADR-010: Keep the canonical array and Problem Details contract stable.
requirements: RF-002: List all tasks with 200 and ascending id ordering.
RF-003: Filter by pendente or concluida and reject an invalid filter.
RN-004: Keep status within the two-value domain.
RN-008: Invalid filters return 400 without task data.
SEC-003: Validate request input before database work and parameterize values.

title: ListTasks: ordered listing and status filtering

description: Implement the CompleteTask vertical slice for PATCH /tasks/{id}/complete. Parse a positive id, execute a parameterized idempotent completion update, return the resulting task with status concluida, distinguish a missing row as 404, and test repeated completion without duplication.

acceptance: Completing an existing pending task returns 200 with status concluida and persists the state.
Repeating completion on the same task returns 200 with the same task and makes no duplicate row.
A nonexistent id returns 404 Problem Details and leaves every task unchanged.
constraints: The slice owns id parsing, UPDATE SQL, affected-row handling, and explicit task mapping.
Use a parameterized long id, await/await using, and the request cancellation token; do not add reopening or concurrency semantics.
A third status value must never be produced.
decisions: ADR-001: Keep completion behavior and SQL in its own vertical slice.
ADR-003: Use direct parameterized Npgsql commands.
ADR-010: Use 200 for idempotent success and Problem Details for 404.
requirements: RF-004: Complete a task through PATCH /tasks/{id}/complete.
RN-004: Persist only pendente or concluida.
RN-005: Completion is idempotent.
RN-007: Missing ids return 404 with no change.
SEC-003: Bind the id as a parameter and avoid unintended mutation.

title: CompleteTask: idempotent state transition

description: Implement the EditTask vertical slice for PUT /tasks/{id}. Trim and validate titulo before mutation, update only the title with parameterized SQL, return the updated task while preserving its current status, distinguish invalid input from a missing id, and cover pending and completed tasks.

acceptance: PUT /tasks/{id} with a valid title returns 200 and persists the trimmed title.
Editing a pending or completed task preserves its existing status.
A missing, empty, or whitespace-only title returns 400 before mutation; a nonexistent id returns 404 and the previous data remains unchanged.
constraints: The slice owns title validation, UPDATE SQL, affected-row handling, and row mapping.
Use long ids and parameterized values, validate before opening a mutable command, and use cancellation-aware async operations.
Do not add title uniqueness, maximum length, version history, or strong concurrency behavior.
decisions: ADR-001: Keep title-edit rules and data access in the EditTask slice.
ADR-003: Use direct parameterized Npgsql SQL.
ADR-010: Return canonical task JSON and Problem Details for 400/404.
requirements: RF-005: Edit the title through PUT /tasks/{id}.
RN-001: Trim and reject an empty title.
RN-006: Editing preserves status.
RN-007: Missing ids return 404 with no change.
RN-009: Invalid titles are rejected atomically.
SEC-003: Validate before mutation and parameterize every input.

title: EditTask: change title while preserving status

description: Implement the RemoveTask vertical slice for DELETE /tasks/{id}. Execute a parameterized delete, return 204 with no body for an existing row, return 404 Problem Details for a missing id, and verify that deletion affects only the requested task.

acceptance: Deleting an existing pending or completed task returns 204 with no body and the task no longer appears in listing.
Deleting a nonexistent id returns 404 Problem Details and does not alter other records.
The delete operation uses a parameterized id and affected-row count to distinguish success from absence.
constraints: The slice owns id parsing, DELETE SQL, affected-row handling, and response mapping.
Use long ids, await/await using, cancellation, and no soft-delete, restore, trash, or audit behavior.
No generic repository or service is introduced.
decisions: ADR-001: Keep removal behavior and SQL in the RemoveTask slice.
ADR-003: Use direct parameterized Npgsql SQL.
ADR-010: Return 204 with no body or sanitized 404 Problem Details.
requirements: RF-006: Remove an existing task through DELETE /tasks/{id}.
RN-007: Missing ids return 404 without mutation.
SEC-003: Parameterize the id and detect affected-row count before reporting success.

title: RemoveTask: delete a task safely

description: Build the real integration-test harness and quality gate around the endpoint slices. Use xUnit with an in-process ASP.NET host, HttpClient, and real Compose Postgres; keep integration tests serial, truncate tasks and reset identity before each case, and cover every endpoint's success and failure contract alongside pure rule tests.

acceptance: Every RF-001 through RF-006 endpoint scenario has a passing integration test over real HTTP and Postgres, including invalid input, missing ids, ordering, repeated completion, and empty results.
Pure tests cover validation/normalization, status domain, filtering, idempotency, mapping, and affected-row decisions without HTTP or Postgres.
Integration cases pass individually, as a suite, and across consecutive runs without ordering or leftover-state dependence.
constraints: Use xUnit, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk, and an ASP.NET test host; mocks and in-memory persistence are not substitutes for integration coverage.
Use a non-parallel integration collection and truncate tasks plus reset its identity sequence before every case through a dedicated test connection.
The test suite must assert status codes, response bodies, and application/problem+json content type for errors.
decisions: ADR-007: Use separate pure unit tests and real HTTP/Postgres integration tests.
ADR-008: Use serial integration execution with deterministic truncate/reset isolation.
ADR-001: Preserve visible ownership of each endpoint's tests by its slice.
requirements: RNF-001: Achieve full real integration coverage for the endpoint scenarios.
RNF-002: Achieve full applicable pure-rule unit coverage.
RNF-003: Prove individual, suite, and repeated-run isolation.
SEC-003: Assert that invalid input is rejected before database mutation.

title: Verification harness: real HTTP/Postgres coverage and deterministic isolation

description: Add resilience proofs for API-only restart, retained-volume persistence, dependency failure sanitization, and log redaction. Recreate the API host while leaving Postgres running, verify id/title/status equality, and assert that responses and captured logs omit credentials, connection details, stack traces, driver messages, payloads, and titles.

acceptance: A task's id, normalized titulo, and status are identical after the API host is recreated while Postgres and its volume remain running.
An unavailable database returns application/problem+json with 503 and none of the connection, credential, internal-host, stack-trace, or driver details.
Failure scenarios and normal test logs contain no task titles, request payloads, credentials, or raw driver exceptions.
constraints: Keep the retained-volume guarantee limited to API restart; do not add backup, restore, HA, performance, or external exposure behavior.
Use the same public contracts and real local dependencies; do not weaken tests by matching only textual PASS output.
Redaction must be verified in both response body/headers and captured logs.
decisions: ADR-005: Prove persistence by recreating the API while retaining the Compose Postgres volume.
ADR-006: Keep failure handling and logging sanitized at the shared boundary.
ADR-007: Exercise resilience through the real integration host and database.
requirements: RN-010: Preserve task identity, normalized title, and status across an API-only restart.
RNF-006: Make persistence after host recreation observable through a query.
RNF-010: Retain data in the Postgres volume across API restarts.
SEC-001: Sanitize database-unavailable responses.
SEC-005: Keep titles and sensitive internal details out of logs.

title: Persistence and resilience: restart proof and sanitized failures

description: Finish the reproducible local development flow with an idempotent init.sh and one aggregate verification command. Bring up and wait for Compose health, run both unit and integration suites, propagate a non-zero result from either suite, verify repeated startup, and document the supported local-only boundary and execution steps.

acceptance: Two successive init.sh executions bring up or reuse healthy Postgres and run the complete unit and integration verification without manual cleanup.
The aggregate command returns success only when both suites pass and returns non-zero when either suite is induced to fail; it does not infer success from textual PASS output.
README documents pinned versions, TODO_DB_CONNECTION override, health/readiness flow, API-only persistence guarantee, unauthenticated local-only use, and out-of-scope production/external exposure.
constraints: init.sh owns Compose readiness and the aggregate command; Compose remains limited to Postgres.
The flow must be idempotent and must not hardcode credentials or log connection strings, titles, payloads, stack traces, or driver details.
No CI, cloud, production deployment, frontend, authentication, migration compatibility, pagination, SLA, or regulated-data claim is added.
decisions: ADR-004: Use Docker Compose as the local Postgres orchestration boundary.
ADR-005: Use a healthcheck and idempotent init flow for readiness and schema setup.
ADR-009: Keep connection configuration environment-based with a local-only default.
ADR-007: Aggregate the unit and real integration suites as the verification result.
requirements: RF-009: Provide Compose, idempotent init.sh, readiness, and one aggregate verification command.
RNF-004: Prove idempotent startup across two successive runs.
RNF-007: Make the aggregate result fail when either suite fails.
RNF-011: Document and verify the reproducible supported environment.
SEC-002: Keep connection configuration externalized.
SEC-004: Document the unauthenticated local-only boundary.

title: Aggregate local verification and idempotent development flow
